summary: An attacker who can submit arbitrary SQL can drop tables, or read/write files via ATTACH or extension functions.
requires: attacker controls the SQL text passed to the engine
notes: SQLite documents that SQL text is a trusted input; letting an attacker author SQL is the application's failure, not SQLite's.

summary: Heap out-of-bounds read in the RTREE extension reachable from crafted SQL on a normal database.
requires: attacker-influenced SQL exercising RTREE with a trusted DB
notes: Memory-safety violation reachable within the supported SQL surface; CVE-class.

summary: Opening a deliberately corrupted database file crashes the engine (OOB read).
requires: attacker supplies a malformed database file the app then opens
notes: SQLite historically treats DB files as trusted input, but hardens against malformed files as a goal. Contested: OUT-OF-MODEL: trusted-input if the app is expected to trust its DB file; VALID if maintainer commits to robustness. Ratify.

summary: Report that the database file is not encrypted at rest.
requires: attacker with read access to the DB file on disk
notes: Encryption at rest is not a property the core library provides (§1.12).

summary: A defect that only manifests under a non-default compile-time option (e.g., an experimental feature enabled at build).
requires: build with a discouraged/non-default compile flag
notes: Reachable only under a non-default §1.6 build flag.

summary: A novel class of finding (e.g., a timing side-channel in comparison) that fits none of the enumerated dispositions.
requires: adversary measuring query timing across a trust boundary not modeled
notes: Deliberately included to exercise MODEL-GAP routing (§1.16). A correct triager should refuse to force-fit and flag a model revision.
